citeAs: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu (2024). Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors. Speech Communication.
creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, Éric Bavu
description: Vibravox is a dataset containing audio recordings of French speech using five different body-conduction audio sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone) and an airborne microphone used as a reference.
name: Vibravox
publisher: Conservatoire national des arts et métiers (Cnam)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The text utilized for participant readings originates from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice. Textual filters were applied to exclude most proper names, numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, or syntactic errors. The text was normalized (lowercased, punctuation removed except apostrophes). Phonetic transcription was generated using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) via the text phonemizer of the CoML lab, followed by manual phonetic transcription for unrecognized words.
rai:dataCollection: A total of 200 participants contributed to the dataset. The recording process consists of four steps: speech-clean (participant reads sentences for 15 minutes), speechless-noisy (participant remains silent in a noisy environment for 2 minutes and 24 seconds), speechless-clean (54 seconds in complete silence), and speech-noisy (54 seconds of speech in a noisy environment).
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone) and an airborne microphone. Recorded simultaneously at a sampling rate of 48 kHz and a resolution of 32 bits.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A 20 Hz high-pass filter is uniformly applied to each acquisition channel. A series of three automatic filters were applied to remove utterances with obvious deficiencies (PER > 10%, SNR <= 1.5 dB, or Lspeech50 <= Lsilence50). Timestamps generated by Voice Activity Detection (VAD) are extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides, and audio is trimmed by 15 ms if timestamps exceed audio boundaries.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Textual filters excluded most proper names, retaining only common first names, French town or region names, and country names. Utterances containing numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, or syntactic errors were removed. Text was lowercased and punctuation removed except for apostrophes.
rai:dataUseCases: Bandwidth extension, speech recognition, and speaker verification.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: whisper-timestamped model, text phonemizer of the CoML lab
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Biometric information (speaker identity, heart rate, breathing) captured by the sensors.
